arc:position-deletes:v2.notes: Arc never writes Iceberg delete files of any kind. Its reconciler only adds and removes whole data files by path (ReplaceDataFiles / AddFiles), and its own row-level DELETE API rewrites the affected Parquet file instead of recording a delete. Nothing in internal/iceberg constructs a position delete file.
caveats: Row-level deletes happen in Arc's storage layer, not as Iceberg delete files

arc:position-deletes:v3.notes: Arc produces Iceberg format-version 2 tables only. The exporter calls iceberg-go v0.6.0's CreateTable without a format-version property, so tables are created at the library default (2), and no code path upgrades a table afterwards -- every metadata.json written by a live Arc 26.09.3 instance carries "format-version": 2. Arc therefore neither writes nor reads a V3 table, so every V3 cell is none rather than a per-feature judgement.
caveats: Arc writes format-version 2 tables; it has no V3 writer and no Iceberg reader at all

arc:equality-deletes:v2.notes: Not supported. Arc has no equality-delete writer; the export path registers and deregisters data files only.

arc:copy-on-write:v2.notes: Arc's row-level DELETE (POST /api/v1/delete with a WHERE clause) rewrites each affected Parquet file without the deleted rows, and the next reconcile pass re-registers that path in one commit, so the table's record counts and column bounds follow the rewrite -- copy-on-write semantics, delivered through Arc's own API rather than Iceberg DML. Verified live: deleting 1 of 7 rows produced a reregistered=1 reconcile and DuckDB's iceberg_scan then returned 6 rows with the manifest record count updated. Partial, not full, because the rewrite reuses the original file path instead of writing a new data file, so earlier snapshots keep pointing at a path whose contents have changed (time travel to a pre-delete snapshot returned the post-delete row count), and because only DELETE drives it -- there is no UPDATE or MERGE.
caveats: Driven by Arc's delete API, not by Iceberg DML -- an external engine cannot trigger it
The rewritten file keeps its original path, so pre-delete snapshots silently reflect the new contents
Eventually consistent: the table converges within one iceberg.reconcile_interval (default 300 s)

arc:schema-evolution:v2.notes: Additive only, and automatic. Arc derives each measurement's column superset from the Parquet footers and evolveSchema adds any missing column as an optional field, then refreshes schema.name-mapping.default from the post-evolution schema (Arc's Parquet carries no field IDs, so without that mapping external readers fail on the new column). Verified live: a measurement that gained a 'temp' field produced schema-id 1 with temp as optional field-id 5 and an extended name mapping. No drop, rename, reorder or type change -- a changed column type is refused outright with the measurement left at its last good state.
caveats: Add-column only: no drop, rename, reorder or promotion
A column whose type changes fails that measurement's export until the source data is fixed
Evolution is inferred from the data, not requested through DDL

arc:table-creation:v2.notes: Arc creates the namespace and the table itself, with no operator DDL: on first sight of a measurement the exporter calls CreateNamespace + CreateTable with the schema derived from the measurement's Parquet, a day(time) partition spec and the metadata-retention properties (write.metadata.delete-after-commit.enabled, write.metadata.previous-versions-max). One table per database/measurement, named <namespace_prefix>_<database>.<measurement>. Partial because there is no CREATE TABLE surface at all: schema, partitioning, properties and naming are fixed by Arc, and you cannot create an Iceberg table that Arc does not own.
caveats: No CREATE TABLE statement or API -- tables appear automatically per measurement
Schema, partition spec and table properties are not operator-configurable

arc:hidden-partitioning:v2.notes: Tables are created with exactly one hidden partition field -- day(time), field-id 1000, name time_day -- and iceberg-go infers each registered file's partition value from the Parquet time min/max. Verified live: the manifest entry for a registered file carried partition {time_day: 20732}. Partial because the transform is hard-coded (day() matches both Arc's hourly files and its daily-compacted files; hour() would reject the latter): no bucket, truncate, month or year, no choice of source column, and a file whose rows straddle a UTC day boundary cannot be mapped at all and is logged and left out of the table.
caveats: day(time) only -- not configurable, and no other transform is available
A data file straddling a UTC day boundary is skipped and excluded from the table

arc:time-travel:v2.notes: Arc has no Iceberg read path, so it cannot query a snapshot by id or timestamp. The snapshots it commits are readable by other engines, but with a caveat Arc users should know: because its delete path rewrites a data file in place at the same path, a pre-delete snapshot resolves to the post-delete file. Verified live -- DuckDB's iceberg_scan(..., snapshot_from_id => <first snapshot>) returned 4 rows for a snapshot committed when the file held 5.
caveats: Arc cannot read Iceberg tables, including its own
In-place file rewrites make historical snapshots non-reproducible across a delete

arc:table-maintenance:v2.notes: Snapshot and metadata retention are built in and run on the reconcile timer: ExpireSnapshots with retain-last = iceberg.retain_snapshots (default 10) and an always-satisfied age gate, plus pruning of the Hadoop-style v<N>.metadata.json copies and iceberg-go's own metadata log. Verified live with retain_snapshots = 1: snapshot history collapsed to 1 and only two v<N>.metadata.json copies remained (retain+1, kept deliberately for directory readers mid-resolve). Data-file compaction is Arc's own, not Iceberg's -- compacted output replaces its sources in the table on the next pass. No orphan-file removal, no rewrite-manifests, no rewrite-data-files: expiry deliberately runs with post-commit cleanup disabled so the exporter can never delete Arc's primary data files, which also means expired manifests and manifest lists are left behind (15 .avro files for 1 live snapshot in the live run).
caveats: No orphan-file removal or rewrite-manifests; expired manifests/manifest-lists are not reclaimed
Compaction is Arc's own file-level compaction reflected into the table, not Iceberg rewrite-data-files
Maintenance is timer-driven configuration, not callable procedures

Arc queries its own Parquet directly; Iceberg is an export surface for other engines.
caveats: iceberg_scan / iceberg_metadata / iceberg_snapshots are rejected by Arc's SQL validator
Arc is a producer of Iceberg tables, not an Iceberg query engine

arc:write-insert:v2.notes: Data lands in the table without rewriting a byte: a background reconciler diffs the measurement's Parquet file set against the table's current data files and commits the delta with AddFiles / ReplaceDataFiles, so Arc's existing files are registered in place (add_files semantics, zero copy). Verified live: ingesting rows produced a snapshot with added-data-files 1 / added-records 5, and DuckDB's iceberg_scan returned them. Rated partial rather than full because this is not an insert interface: there is no INSERT statement or append API, the table is a mirror of Arc's own file set for a measurement Arc ingested, and Arc cannot append to a table it does not own. Append is also eventually consistent -- up to iceberg.reconcile_interval (default 300 s) behind live ingest.
caveats: No INSERT or append API; writes enter through Arc's own ingest path and appear on the reconcile timer
Only tables Arc owns -- Arc cannot write into an externally created Iceberg table
Up to iceberg.reconcile_interval (default 300 s) behind live ingest

No UPDATE, no MERGE INTO, and no Iceberg-level DML surface: an external engine holding the table cannot mutate it.

arc:catalog-integration:v2.notes: One catalog, embedded and not pluggable: Arc keeps table pointers in an iceberg-go SQL catalog on its own SQLite database (the same file as auth/tiering by default, or iceberg.catalog_db_path). PyIceberg reads it directly as a SqlCatalog. For engines without a SQLite catalog client Arc also publishes the Hadoop-style discovery files next to each table's metadata -- version-hint.text plus a v<N>.metadata.json copy -- so directory-based readers resolve the current snapshot without being handed a filename; verified live with DuckDB's iceberg_scan against the table directory. There is no REST, Glue, Hive, Nessie or JDBC-over-Postgres option, so a shared multi-engine catalog has to be layered in front of the warehouse by the operator.
caveats: Embedded SQLite SQL catalog only -- the catalog implementation is not configurable
Directory-based readers are served by version-hint.text + v<N>.metadata.json
Table metadata references data files by absolute path, so a local warehouse is not portable between hosts

caveats: No NDV sketches (Puffin) -- Parquet footers carry no distinct counts

caveats: The catalog implementation is not configurable (iceberg.catalog_db_path only moves the SQLite file)

arc:unknown-type:v2.notes: A V3 type; not present in Arc's type mapping.

arc:unknown-type:v3.notes: Arc produces Iceberg format-version 2 tables only. The exporter calls iceberg-go v0.6.0's CreateTable without a format-version property, so tables are created at the library default (2), and no code path upgrades a table afterwards -- every metadata.json written by a live Arc 26.09.3 instance carries "format-version": 2. Arc therefore neither writes nor reads a V3 table, so every V3 cell is none rather than a per-feature judgement.
caveats: Arc writes format-version 2 tables; it has no V3 writer and no Iceberg reader at all

arc:lineage:v2.notes: A V3 feature. Arc assigns no _row_id or _last_updated_sequence_number -- it registers Parquet files written by its ingest path, which carry no lineage columns.
